title: Mashed Potatoes – Chunky, Red, Delicious
description: Food & Wine: Our No. 1 Mashed Potato Recipe of All Time – No peeler needed here! These mashed red potatoes are for the cooks who crave a little texture (or who just don't want to be bothered with a potato peeler). Boil the potatoes with skins on, then mash with butter and milk for a creamy but lightly chunky side dish swirled with pretty flecks of red. Here, we also include thinly sliced scallions for an additional pop of color and flavor to finish the delicious red potato mash.
ingredients: 6 pounds red potatoes, scrubbed and cut into 2-inch chunks
2 cups milk, warmed (maybe with some sour cream or Crème Fraiche)
directions: Put the potatoes in a large pot and cover with water. Cover the pot and bring to a boil. Add a large pinch of salt and boil, uncovered, over moderately high heat, until fork tender, about 20 to 25 minutes.
Drain the potatoes and return to the pot.
Shake the pot over moderately high heat to dry the potatoes. Off the heat, lightly mash the potatoes.
Add the softened butter and warmed milk and optional garlic powder; mash until incorporated.
Stir in the scallions, season with salt and pepper.
notes:
Make ahead:
These mashed red potatoes can be made early in the day. Cover and keep warm, then reheat gently, adding more warm milk if the potatoes seem stiff.
